correctness.rationale: For any reduced common-denominator GBC, the polynomial normalization and affine-precision identities show every facet equation fails to divide q: otherwise all vertex numerators vanish on that facet and share a nontrivial factor. Nonadjacent facet-line intersections are zeros of every numerator, hence of q. On each side there are m-3 distinct finite residual points except that one parallel mate can eliminate exactly one, forcing deg q >=m-4 and >=m-3 on any unpaired side. The exact Wachspress restriction formula a|Li=k_i k_(i+1) product(nonadjacent facet forms)|Li follows by direct endpoint calculation and shows a(Vi)>0. For all-paired sides, any degree-(m-4) q is locally proportional to a, proportionality constants agree at polygon vertices, and q-c*a has degree <m yet is divisible by all m distinct supporting lines, hence is zero. This excludes lower denominators for all polygons; the already-proved planar adjoint-degree dichotomy identifies the exact branches. An executable exact-SymPy source checks all proof-specific polynomial identities and six geometric configurations, including a difficult noncentral parallel-paired hexagon. Limits: computational examples are supplemental, not a proof for arbitrary m.

originality.rationale: Baumbach–Winter arXiv:2611.02110v1 explicitly leaves deg(P)>=m-2d as Conjecture 4.1 and does not classify minimum denominator degree for all polygons. The 2025 Baumbach–Freyer–Weigert–Winter result determines the degree of the fixed Wachspress adjoint, not optimality against arbitrary other rational coordinate systems. Kohn–Ranestad 2019 gives projective adjoint uniqueness under simple-arrangement hypotheses, strongly relevant to generic polygons but not, as stated, the full nongeneric/parallel case. A direct original proof of denominator minimality and borderline-denominator rigidity covers all convex m-gons, particularly noncentrally symmetric parallel-paired cases. Neither targeted literature searches nor mathematical research-index comparisons disclosed equal or broader coverage. Priority remains best-knowledge, not absolute.
residual_risks: Older algebraic interpolation literature could encode an equivalent global minimum-denominator statement without using barycentric terminology; targeted searches cannot establish absolute historical priority.
Kohn–Ranestad generic-projective uniqueness is strong and may already imply a nondegenerate special case; the novel scope is the unconditional result and parallel-paired degeneration.
The exact formula for the fixed adjoint degree is relied upon from the cited 2025 published preprint and not reproved here.

value.rationale: The result settles the planar case of a specifically stated recent open denominator-degree conjecture, and improves a conjectural lower bound to an exact all-polygons classification. The equality of minimal denominator and Wachspress adjoint degree is a structural rigidity theorem, not a direct degree count of a chosen construction. The challenging case with all side directions paired but no center of symmetry cannot be handled by the m-4 elementary root count alone, requiring a novel vertex-gluing argument. The invariant governs rational basis complexity in polygon interpolation; classification is motivated and plausibly reusable.
